edges.mechanism: Phylloquinone bypasses VKOR inhibition and restores carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX, X; antagonizes warfarin and large doses induce temporary resistance.
edges.evidence: FDA label; RCTs of 100-200 ug/d low-dose K showed small TTR gain (+3.5%) and fewer INR excursions but no clinical-outcome benefit; uncontrolled starts/stops shift INR.

edges.mechanism: Same VKOR-antagonism reversal as warfarin; 1 mg oral K1 over-reversed acenocoumarol INR.
edges.evidence: RCTs: phenprocoumon + 100 ug/d K improved stability (RR maximal stability 1.8); acenocoumarol reversal RCT showed over-correction (RR 1.83).

edges.mechanism: DOACs inhibit factor Xa/IIa directly, independent of the vitamin K cycle; no vitamin K-mediated interaction expected and K1 does not reverse DOACs.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic reviews; DOACs also falsely elevate PT/INR, so INR is not a valid marker on DOACs.

edges.mechanism: Phytonadione does not counteract heparin's anticoagulant action.
edges.evidence: FDA label statement.

edges.mechanism: NMTT/methyl-thiadiazole side chains inhibit hepatic vitamin K epoxide reductase; hypoprothrombinemia in patients with low vitamin K status (e.g. TPN), reversible with K1.
edges.evidence: Clinical pharmacology study and reviews; label indication for antibacterial-induced hypoprothrombinemia.

edges.mechanism: Lipase inhibition reduces fat-soluble vitamin absorption, including vitamin K; may alter warfarin response.
edges.evidence: Small open-label study (non-significant fall in vitamin K) and a case report of raised INR on warfarin.

edges.mechanism: Cholestyramine binds bile acids, reducing absorption of fat-soluble vitamins; vitamin K-deficiency coagulopathy reported.
edges.evidence: Case reports, including deficiency refractory to concurrent oral vitamin K.

edges.mechanism: Theoretical reduction of fat-soluble vitamin absorption with prolonged use.
edges.evidence: Case-level evidence only; literature support described as weak.

edges.mechanism: High-dose salicylates can cause hypoprothrombinemia by interfering with vitamin K metabolism; phytonadione is labeled for this.
edges.evidence: FDA label indication; no supplement-specific trials.

edges.mechanism: High-dose alpha-tocopherol antagonizes vitamin K-dependent carboxylation, raising PIVKA-II.
edges.evidence: Two 12-wk RCT cohorts (1000 IU/d) showed PIVKA-II increases; IOM describes E-K antagonism as established.

edges.mechanism: Additive vitamin K activity; MK-7 has long half-life and accumulates 7-8 fold, so combined intake changes VKA response.
edges.evidence: Human PK/PD comparison study; >=50 ug/d MK-7 may interfere with oral anticoagulants.

edges.mechanism: Phylloquinone is converted to tissue MK-4 (via menadione/UBIAD1); both are catabolized by CYP4F2; additive vitamin K load.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic review, human lactation supplementation study, in vitro enzymology.

edges.mechanism: Vitamin D/calcium plus K1 may add modestly to bone mineral effects via osteocalcin carboxylation.
edges.evidence: RCTs: benefit only in combined arms (ultradistal radius; femoral neck +1.7%); network MA ranks D+K highest for P1NP/OC.

edges.with: fat malabsorption (cholestasis, celiac, IBD, cystic fibrosis)
edges.mechanism: Bile-dependent absorption; deficiency and hypoprothrombinemia risk; oral K1 needs bile salts if bile deficient.
edges.evidence: FDA label indications; RCT in Crohn's disease corrected %ucOC with 1 mg/d.

edges.mechanism: Low vitamin K intake/status and high dp-ucMGP; K1 corrects markers but calcification/outcome benefit unproven.
edges.evidence: Small RCTs and MAs: K1 lowers dp-ucMGP more than K2; no mortality effect; mild serum calcium rise.

edges.with: hypersensitivity to phytonadione or castor-oil/polysorbate solubilizer
edges.mechanism: Non-IgE anaphylactoid reactions to parenteral (esp. IV/IM) phytonadione, linked to solubilizers; fatal cases.
edges.evidence: FDA boxed warning; incidence ~3/10,000 IV doses.

edges.mechanism: Benzyl alcohol preservative can cause fatal gasping syndrome in neonates and infants; use preservative-free phytonadione.
edges.evidence: FDA label warning.

edges.mechanism: K1 intake lowers undercarboxylated prothrombin (PIVKA-II); VKAs and high-dose vitamin E raise it; PIVKA-II also used as an HCC marker.
edges.evidence: Lab-medicine review; RCT of vitamin E.

edges.mechanism: K1 lowers INR in VKA-treated patients; PT/INR is insensitive as a vitamin K status marker.
edges.evidence: Label and RCTs of INR reversal; lab-medicine review.

edges.mechanism: Supplementation suppresses %ucOC and dp-ucMGP, which are status markers, not outcomes.
edges.evidence: RCTs: %ucOC lower with 500 ug/d; dp-ucMGP -86% with 10 mg thrice weekly.

edges.mechanism: Reduced CYP4F2 K1 omega-hydroxylase activity raises hepatic K1; carriers need higher coumarin doses.
edges.evidence: In vitro human liver data; MA of 30 studies: +8.3% coumarin dose in T carriers.

edges.mechanism: Lower VKOR expression increases warfarin sensitivity regardless of vitamin K level; risk alleles modestly associated with low BMD.
edges.evidence: Gene-nutrient modeling study; MA of 6 studies (OR 1.16).
